newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore opens bunker to mark WW2 anniversary.
newsitem.headline: Singapore opens bunker to mark WW2 anniversary.

text.p: Singapore on Saturday marks the 55th anniversary of its fall to Japanese forces during World War Two by opening the so-called Battle Box -- an underground operation centre used by the British Army that was sealed for over 40 years.

Speaking at the opening ceremony, Defence Minister Tony Tan said: "the lesson to learn is that we may have friends and allies, but ultimately the defence of our country is our own responsibility. And we must have the resources and capability to carry out that responsibility."

The bunker, refurbished at a cost of Singapore $3 million, was one of the most extensive underground operation complexes built by the British in Singapore. First completed in 1939, the 22-room bomb-proof bunker is about six metres (yards) down and nine metres long.
It was used by the British as a command headquarters for the defence of Singapore, then headed by Lieutenant-General Arthur Percival.
Walking through the tunnel, visitors can hear the sound of air-raid sirens as 24 life-sized wax figures dressed as British officers depict the activities that took place there between 1939 and 1942.
It was also there that the British Army decided on 15 February 1942 to surrender to the Japanese.
